source.title: ZENITH: Automated Gradient Norm Informed Stochastic Optimization

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the paper and appendices. It is labelled arXiv:2601.15212v2 [cs.LG] 1 Jul 2026; no relevant truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests learning-rate schedulers and their effects on test accuracy, sharpness, and training time, but it does not test whether networks that fit random labels generalize, the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, width, sharpness-measure, or memorized-example claims. Its discussion of flat minima and generalization concerns a different intervention and measure.
record.gate_note: No reported result measures generalization gaps between training and test error for the claim versions. The paper reports test accuracy/RMSE under scheduler comparisons and correlations between learning rate, Hessian top eigenvalue, and test accuracy. Its generalization-gap discussion is a theoretical argument, not a measured gap result. Scheduler and baseline results are outside the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates learning-rate schedulers, but its results do not test V1–V8. Its closest result relates unscaled Hessian sharpness to test accuracy, whereas V7 concerns magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures. Applying schedules to adaptive optimizers does not supply the adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison required by V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ZENITH achieves strong performance among automatic learning-rate schedulers with reduced wall-clock training time, and attribute its success partly to reaching flatter minima with little computational overhead. The flatness explanation is their interpretation, supported by correlations and a conditional theoretical argument.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates an automated learning-rate scheduler; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports test-performance sensitivity to initial learning rate, window size, regularization strength, dataset, and base optimizer, but these results do not measure the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 3–5 report scheduler accuracy–time comparisons. ZENITH achieves 92.91% CIFAR-10 accuracy versus 92.69% for vanilla SGD, with respective times of 15.84 and 28.42 minutes. These are selected instantaneous accuracy–time combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-norm-based learning-rate scheduling can improve observed accuracy–time trade-offs relative to selected schedulers and constant-rate SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 associates higher constant learning rates with smaller Hessian top eigenvalues and higher test accuracy; scheduler comparisons show a similar association. Training losses also differ. Appendix B derives a conditional loss-gap argument using an assumed shift between training and test optima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian sharpness is associated with test accuracy in the reported scheduler experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 reports improved CIFAR-100 test accuracy when ZENITH is added to Adam, Adamax, and Adagrad. It does not report the controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison required by V4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers can benefit from a separate long-term learning-rate schedule.

record.code_released: The PyTorch and TensorFlow implementations and reproduction notebooks will be made available upon acceptance; no URL stated.
record.problems: No experiments manipulate or measure random-label memorization, training-to-test error gaps, width beyond interpolation, or memorized-example removal. Flatness/generalization is argued theoretically and illustrated through test-accuracy comparisons; the paper does not report a direct measured generalization-gap outcome. Several relevant comparisons are shown in figures, and the supplied text does not include supplementary material beyond the included appendices.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows for V1–V8: the study's scheduler-performance and sharpness results do not measure the outcomes named by those versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including switching optimizers and decoupled weight decay.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The empty qualifying row set is appropriate. The record's relation of tests conflicts with its own explanation and should be discusses. No verdict follows from the related sharpness results because they do not measure V7's specified construct.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; all specified models and conditions.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap rankings and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
